figures.caption: FIGURE 1 Overview of the coupled degradation modes of layered oxide cathodes in ASSLBs. Bulk and interfacial failure modes—mechanical degradation, space-charge-layer formation, element interdiffusion, structural phase transitions, chemical decomposition, and oxygen-redox instability— operate simultaneously within the composite cathode (center), are compounded by its microstructural complexity, and are increasingly amenable to AI/ML-based prediction. These coupled failure modes motivate the multiscale, diagnostics-driven framework developed in this review.

figures.caption: FIGURE 9 Unified multiscale degradation map of layered oxide cathodes in ASSLBs. Each row pairs, at a given length scale, representative diagnostic outputs with the degradation phenomena they resolve: cation disorder, phase transitions, and oxygen instability at the atomic scale; CEI formation and surface decomposition at the nanoscale; cracking, void formation, and contact loss at the microscale; lithium-concentration gradients and space-charge-layer-induced polarization at the meso/electrode scale; and capacity fade, impedance rise, and premature failure at the macroscopic cell level. The ascending arrow indicates how lower-scale instabilities propagate upward into cell-level performance loss. The mitigation strategies informed by these diagnostics are consolidated in Table 4, completing the Diagnosis →Mechanism →Mitigation linkage.

figures.caption: FIGURE 12 Suggested future research directions aimed at addressing current diagnostic limitations and advancing cathode design for ASSLBs: stress-resilient cathodes and composite cathode engineering (validating the mitigations of Table 4 under the practical conditions of Section 5.1), self- healing interfaces, advanced manufacturing of well-crystallized cathode particles, integrated operando platforms for real-time multimodal diagnostics (Controversies 1 and 2, Section 5.2), and AI/ML multiscale modeling supported by the required data standardization (Controversies 4 and 5, Section 5.2). Together, these advances can enable broader applications of ASSLBs in electric vehicles, drones, robotic systems, air taxis, and stationary energy storage.
